# llms.txt — creation-space (Creativity Research)

> This file helps AI assistants and language models understand the structure and content of this site.

## Site Overview

This is the research site of pjdhiro exploring **what creation is** — structural similarity patterns in creative processes across 30 academic domains.

- **Primary Language**: Japanese (日本語), with English summaries
- **Site URL**: https://uminomae.github.io/project-design-theory/cs/
- **Topics**: Creativity, Five-Stage Model, Structural Patterns, Cross-Domain Analysis, Negative Capability

## Core Concepts

### Five-Stage Model of Creation (創造の5段階モデル)

Field (場) → Wave (波) → Edge (縁) → Vortex (渦) → Bundle (束)

- Field (場): A stable state, like the sea before waves rise. A starting point in theory.
- Wave (波): Differences arise in the field and rise as a sway. The situation changes; the differences part and face each other.
- Edge (縁): The border where different things meet and collide. New relations and rules arise there. (Not the "edge of chaos" of complexity science.)
- Vortex (渦): Rises as one whole. The two remain distinguishable, yet it is as if they were one.
- Bundle (束): Vortices affect one another and remain together as a new form. It becomes the next field.

The five stages do not always proceed in order; they run at the same time and interpenetrate. The definitions are provisional, written in two layers: pjdhiro's own felt sense (the working definition above), and features other theories report ("other accounts describe cases like this"). Features found in the survey of 30 academic domains are discussed and built in to strengthen the definition. The canonical source is `knowledge/schema/five-stages.md`.

### Cross-Domain Structural Similarity

The project investigates whether the structure of creation — not just the content — follows common patterns across radically different fields, from neuroscience to musicology, from mathematics to performing arts.

## Site Structure

- `index.html` — Main entry point with Three.js visualization
- `/?domain=D01` ~ `/?domain=D30` — The record of each domain, checked against primary sources
- `/?modal=domains` — Opens the overview of the 30 domains
- The records are Markdown files in this site (`evidence/evidence-Dxx-*.md`, listed below)
- Earlier versions (reader guides, cross-domain synthesis, cross-domain themes and their verification, survey overview) were written before the claims were checked against primary sources. They were withdrawn from this site on 2026-11-10 and are no longer listed here.

## Research Methodology

Each of the 30 domains is reviewed one at a time. For about ten theories per domain, the original text by the proposer (or by an author of the same theory) is located and read, and the claims made about the theory are checked against that text. Each record lists what was read, where it was read, and the verification status of each source. Theories whose original text could not be read are kept apart from the main table and are not counted. The records are written by Claude (AI) and may contain errors.
